name: Keep houseplants alive
blurb: Almost every houseplant death is overwatering, wrong light, or the plant being in the wrong room. Get those three right and most plants look after themselves.
gear: A few forgiving plants: pothos, snake plant, ZZ, spider plant
Pots with drainage holes, without exception
A watering can and a moisture meter or your finger
steps: Match plant to light honestly: watch a spot through a day before putting anything in it. "Bright indirect" means bright, not dark.
Water by checking, not by schedule: push a finger two knuckles into the soil and only water if it is dry.
When you do water, water thoroughly until it runs out the bottom, then empty the saucer. Never leave a pot standing in water.
Learn the symptoms: yellow lower leaves and soggy soil is overwatering; crisp brown edges is underwatering or dry air.
Repot when roots come out of the drainage holes, going up only one pot size.
Feed only during active growth in spring and summer, at half the stated strength.
tips: Pots without drainage holes kill plants. A decorative pot needs an inner pot with drainage.
More houseplants die of kindness than neglect. When in doubt, wait another few days.
proof: Five plants alive and visibly growing a year after you got them.
